video_title: NBL Now Roundtable x Hoop Collective Podcast

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Luke Paul's commitment to Duke University and NBL Next Stars
quotes.excerpt: Luke Paul committed to Duke. He signed a multi-year deal as an NBL Next Star.
quotes.quote: Luke Paul committed to Duke. He signed a multi-year deal as an NBL Next Star, but obviously decided to forgo their second season to commit to Duke University under John Scheyer. He only had one call with them. He did not visit them at all. One call with them. He said he felt it. I spoke to him after. He had calls with other teams. It did not feel anywhere close to his ride as it did with John Scheyer and that staff.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Duke is the right path for Luke Paul's development
quotes.excerpt: If you are going to leap of faith, who would you not want to do it with?
quotes.quote: If you are going to commit to some place in the US, it is a leap of faith. If you are going to leap of faith, who would you not want to do it with other than a program like Duke, for sure? And John Scheyer has routinely shown he is going to get guys drafted very highly. That is the path that Luke is on. Luke is on the path to hopefully having a great development year here in the NBL and then have a great development year where he will be richly rewarded at Duke and then hopefully be a high lottery pick in 2028.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Luke Paul's performance at the U17 World Cup
quotes.excerpt: He was a star at the U17 World Cup in Turkey this summer.
quotes.quote: He was a star at the U17 World Cup in Turkey this summer. If you look at the guys coming out of that, Jojo and Boomje Boomje, who is also committed to Duke, he was dominant for the US in that event, although he spent a lot of his developmental years in Europe. His father played in the NBA and his father sent him to Europe to develop, but he is an American and helped the Americans win that World Cup.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: Luke Paul's impressive stats and shooting ability
quotes.excerpt: He averaged around 15, 6 and 6, shot over 50% from three on volume.
quotes.quote: He averaged around 15, 6 and 6, shot over 50% from three on volume. Super impressive.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: The evolution of the NBL Next Stars program
quotes.excerpt: The Next Stars program was primarily when it started, it was an NBL to NBA pathway.
quotes.quote: The Next Stars program was primarily when it started, it was an NBL to NBA pathway. That is almost exclusively what it was. It then pivoted a little bit. We saw some draft and stash guys come here. We saw guys like Justinian Jessup come through here. We saw draft and stash. Now, because of NIL, it has no choice but to, while it wants to remain an NBL to NBA pathway, it knows that it does have to accept that some guys will come here, especially 17-year-olds who cannot go to college yet, come here as a gap year, be part of their development, and then help, you know, create these good athletes who can then go to college.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Top US high school prospects reclassifying to college
quotes.excerpt: We are seeing top high school kids in the US reclassify, which basically means they are going.
quotes.quote: We are seeing top high school kids in the US reclassify, which basically means they are going to go to the colleges for two years. Both Boomje Boomje and Kutsuritsa are both, they have to go to the college for two years. And Marcus Spears Jr. as well, who is a potential top five pick going to Texas. So three of the top five potential picks and then Luke would sort of be on that path if he was in America, he probably would be at a university this fall.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Luke Paul's potential as an Australian guard
quotes.excerpt: It makes sense, a big Australian guard who can really pass the ball.
quotes.quote: It makes sense, a big Australian guard who can really pass the ball. He can shoot it too now. Well, then we talked to the scouts, they talk about his shot form just looks so good. They are so excited. And Olgun was saying that yesterday too. And you mentioned when we had lunch with you yesterday, like this kid's hands. He has some like softball mitts for hands and I wonder like how much more is this kid going to grow?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Luke Paul to John Stockton
quotes.excerpt: Did his career was defined by the size of his hands. He's got John Stockton's hands.
quotes.quote: Did his career was defined by the size of his hands. He's got John Stockton's hands. His hands are bigger than John Stockton's hands, but Stockton was what, 6'1, 6'2? Luke's already 6'6. He's, I mean, Josh is 6'8. Josh is 6'8. He's headed for, I think, he conservatively at least that size. And already looking terrific on his fundamentals. So it, it looked, it was big news in the US today that he committed to Duke because first off, he wasn't on anybody's radar. And he told me last night that this has stayed quiet for almost a month.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst's relationship with Mike Krzyzewski
quotes.excerpt: I've had great opportunity to spend a lot of time over the years with Mike Krzyzewski.
quotes.quote: I've had great opportunity to spend a lot of time over the years with Mike Krzyzewski because he was a US national team coach and I covered multiple Olympics, multiple World Cups, and he was never anything but terrific to me. I've had, you know, work with so many Duke alums over the years in my profession, Danny Ferry, Elton Brand, Grant Hill, you know, I go on and on. Just all these guys who are just incredible guys. And yet, and yet, if Duke's on, you're rooting for the other team, no matter what.

quotes.speaker: Olgun Uluc
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA players in the NBL and team success
quotes.excerpt: When former NBA guys come here and they don't immediately dominate.
quotes.quote: When former NBA guys come here and they don't immediately dominate. There's not an expectation that, so Javale McGee was here last season. His numbers, individual numbers were good. It didn't lead to team success. Cole Anthony's come here. He's, he's not playing currently. He may end up there, but he's not playing like the best guard in the league. There are guards all across international basketball. There are guards here in the NBL who are unbelievably comfortable in this environment.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Bryce Cotton's dominance in the NBL
quotes.excerpt: You're not going to come into Bryce Cotton's league and push him around.
quotes.quote: You're not going to come into Bryce Cotton's league and push him around. So, I mean, you know, I don't care who you are. I don't care if you're 17 or you're 26 like Cole Anthony is. So, that's, you know, Bryce obviously, if he wanted to, could, could find other pastures, but he has become one of the great players in the history of the of the league. So, he's, you're going to have to contend with guys like that.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The 10th anniversary of the 2014 FIBA World Cup

And I've had great opportunity to spend a lot of time over the years with Mike Krzyzewski because he was a US national team coach and I covered multiple Olympics, multiple World Cups, and he was never anything but terrific to me. I've had, you know, work with so many Duke alums over the years in my profession, Danny Ferry, Elton Brand, Grant Hill, you know, I go on and on. Just all these guys who are just incredible guys. And yet, and yet, if Duke's on, you're rooting for the other team, no matter what.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The French national team's champagne celebration
quotes.excerpt: Every time they scored, they'd order a bottle of champagne for everybody in the whole restaurant.
quotes.quote: Every time they scored, they'd order a bottle of champagne for everybody in the whole restaurant. They were 50 bottles of champagne. And then they score again, I don't know who they played, you know, they score again, 50 more bottles of champagne. And like, they got guys like J.R. Smith saying, I'd never seen anybody spend money like this. Like Kevin Love was like, these guys drop six figures like an hour and a half. And for the French to score another goal, they were going to have to, you know, mortgage their, their, their yacht.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The 2015 Eastern Conference Finals and Andrew Bogut's injury
quotes.excerpt: The blow that undercut them was not Draymond getting suspended. The blow that undercut them was when.
quotes.quote: The blow that undercut them was not Draymond getting suspended. The blow that undercut them was when Bogut hurt his knee in game five. Got run into by J.R. Smith on a drive, sprained his knee. His importance to that team, is particularly their defense, was underscored not by when they won, but what happened when he got hurt. Bogut's injury was, and I don't, I don't mean to, I'd rather talk about his accomplishments, obviously he arrived in in Golden State, people thinking that it was a, it was a disastrous decision. They booed because they were mad they they gave up Monta Ellis. Right. And it's a laughable thing now.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Andrew Bogut's impact on the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: He was one of the coaches who, you know, the way that they defend, they put a.
quotes.quote: He was one of the coaches who, you know, the way that they defend, they put a a four man on him. Sometimes even a three and just try to get under him and and push him around. You know, that's how Will Weaver started playing defense. Um, he had a, he had a, he had a talent deficit, but um, you know, so yeah, I, I, I don't think, I don't think it's an Australian thing. Trust me, when a white American dude gets on the floor, they got a bullseye on them too. You know that.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Andrew Bogut's professional demeanor and resilience
quotes.excerpt: He doesn't get bothered by the officiating. He gets scored on sometimes, doesn't get bothered.
quotes.quote: He doesn't get bothered by the officiating. He gets scored on sometimes, doesn't get bothered. He doesn't complain. You can elbow him, you know, he is totally from the Aussie tradition of not showing injury, not, not, not being intimidated, never backing down. And that demeanor, a lot of young people could in the NBA could benefit from that and not looking to get bailed out by a call every time.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of player movement on NBA rivalries
quotes.excerpt: The best moments in the NBA have been about rivalries.
quotes.quote: The best moments in the NBA have been about rivalries. The Laker-Celtics in the 80s, you know, Michael Jordan having to go through the, the the Pistons in the, in the, in the early 90s. Um, I just, I, I, all the player movement and stuff, I do think it takes away from the rivalries. And the, they, they, they, we'll see how much they've fixed the tanking issues. I'm, you know, I'm concerned about maybe there's tanking of playing in games and whatever, but we'll see about all that. If the goal is to break up teams in small markets, like what, that, that, that doesn't make sense.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial impact of star players taking less money
quotes.excerpt: You got star players like Jaylen Brunson and Victor Wembanyama taking less money for the team.
quotes.quote: You got star players like Jaylen Brunson and Victor Wembanyama taking less money for the team. That's, really good if you're an owner. Like, oh, what do you mean? My superstar player, I don't even have to pay him the max? Look at the value of the teams. Lakers sold 12 months, they sold again for 20% more. The value of the teams are up. The players are taking less, less, you know, some of the players being to take less than their max. If you're an owner, you're like, this is terrific. And that's why it's happening.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The 2021 Tokyo Olympics and the US gold medal
quotes.excerpt: The US has obviously won every gold since 04 in Athens. They qualified for the last two.
quotes.quote: The US has obviously won every gold since 04 in Athens. They qualified for the last two Olympics by that much. And I think 28, it's open. It's wide open. There will be no Steph Curry. You don't have to qualify. Oh, you're talking about the gold medal. Yeah. It is wide open. And look what Steph had to do. I may be biased, but I think he's the most important player over the past 20 years, even over LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The 2021 Tokyo Olympics MVP voting
quotes.excerpt: They gave out an MVP at the Olympics for the first time ever. And the voting on it.
quotes.quote: They gave out an MVP at the Olympics for the first time ever. And the voting on it was a little bit nebulous. We didn't really understand what the voting was. I mean, there was some voters, but I think the vote happened before. Anyway, LeBron won the gold medal. I mean, won the MVP. What? Did you even know that? It wasn't really publicized, but LeBron won the MVP in the Olympics. But also remember Steph didn't have a great Olympics until the lights were brightest. And then he obviously, took over.
